item.title: Free and slave states and territories, 1850 (data for lessons) v0.1
item.snippet: The 31 states, the District of Columbia and the territories of late 1850, in four groups: free state, slave state, free territory, territory open to slavery.
item.description:
The states and territories of the United States in late 1850, after California's admission, made for US History map lessons. Each area has one of four groups and a one-sentence reason. Virginia includes today's West Virginia; Missouri is one area; the area the source labels Oklahoma is Indian Territory.

Outlines are from Esri's digitization of the 1850 plate in Harper's Atlas of American History (1920). That map classes each area by the law that made it free or slave; this layer uses four plain groups instead. Territory boundaries in the West were unsettled in 1850 and are approximate.
